title: Shrink the goal, not the dream
description: A dream can stay big while the next goal gets small. Tiny goals are not a lack of ambition; they are how ambition survives contact with a busy life.

body.heading: Big goals, distant feedback
paragraphs: 'Learn the piano', 'write a book', 'get fit': these are directions, not tasks. They are too large to act on directly, and they give feedback so slowly that motivation starves.
The dream is worth keeping. What it needs is a translator: a next goal small enough to finish this week and clearly connected to the larger direction.

body.heading: Cut until it fits the week
paragraphs: Take the dream and ask: what would the smallest meaningful piece of this look like? One song learned by heart. One page written. One walk after dinner, three times.
Finish that piece, then cut the next one. A chain of small finished goals carries you further than a single heroic goal abandoned in week two, and each link is proof the dream is moving.

takeaway: Keep the dream large and the next step small enough to finish this week.
